anchor_definition: The anchor is the login submit handler recorded as the answer in 1.json (label controllers.js:345 -> the doLogin@329 body). It reads the credentials, base64-encodes the password (password: base64Encode(password)) and assembles + sends the POST /login whose password field is the observed token. The construction path is graded below it: loginService.login (the dedicated /login request builder, 0.7) -> base64Encode (generic base64 primitive that produces the token bytes, 0.5) -> $iq_http.http (generic ajax transport/sink, 0.2). base64Decode is the off-chain inverse; the three sibling doLogin handlers (different login flows) are off-chain lookalike decoys. NOTE: controllers.js holds four near-identical $scope.doLogin handlers; the anchor is specifically the one at offset 8780 (line 329) that drives the captured loginService.login request — pinned by explicit offsets because the four share an identical header.

anchor.why: $scope.doLogin@329, the login handler captured as the 1.json answer: it reads username/password, base64-encodes the password (password: base64Encode(password)), assembles the request data and calls loginService.login -> the POST /login whose password field is the observed base64 token. This is the specific handler matching the captured request, distinct from the three sibling doLogin flows.

roles.why: loginService.login (service.js): the dedicated /login request builder. It assembles the POST params for the login endpoint (url = server()+'login', method POST) carrying the credential payload with the base64 password, then hands them to the generic transport. A target-specific helper nested below the submit handler and above the generic ajax transport.

A generic, keyless base64 encoder (out += base64EncodeChars.charAt(...)) that encodes any string. It computes the observed token bytes but is not bound to the password field — doLogin binds it. Reusable encoding primitive shared across login/register flows; a Core utility below the target-specific request builder.

$iq_http.http (app.min.js): the generic angular $http transport wrapper used by every service method (login, register, validate, ...). It emits the already-built request and returns the promise — the generic ajax sender/sink, not login-specific.
The inverse base64 decoder defined next to base64Encode; never on the password-encoding path. A pure decoy.

Sibling $scope.doLogin@799: a near-identical login handler in a different controller/flow (it base64-encodes the password but drives a different login service call, not the captured POST /login). A strong lookalike decoy, not the handler that produced the observed request.
Sibling $scope.doLogin@1484: a near-identical login handler in a different controller/flow. A strong lookalike decoy, not the captured-request handler.
